title: Punjab Power Strike: Services Disrupted Post-Agitation Withdrawal - The Chenab Times
full_text:
Despite Punjab State Power Corporation Limited (PSPCL) employee unions announcing the withdrawal of their agitation, widespread power disruptions persist in several parts of Punjab, impacting crucial agricultural activities and daily life for millions.
Information was available with The Chenab Times indicating that farmers in regions including Barnala and Nabha have reported ongoing, unaddressed electricity faults. This situation is particularly critical during the ongoing paddy transplantation season, a vital period for agricultural output in the state.
Call for End to Strike
Aman Arora, Punjab Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) president and a Cabinet Minister, made a public appeal on Sunday urging the striking PSPCL employees to immediately cease their industrial action. He emphasized the severe hardship being experienced by farmers during the peak paddy transplantation season and the disruption of essential services for an estimated three crore residents across Punjab.
Arora reiterated the Punjab government’s openness to dialogue, stating that a high-level committee, formed approximately 20 to 25 days prior at the unions’ request, is actively deliberating on their pending demands. He assured that any genuine recommendations from this committee would be considered for acceptance by the government.
Government’s Stance on Demands
Addressing reporters in Sangrur, Arora stated that resorting to strikes that cause public inconvenience and hardship to farmers cannot be justified. He reminded the employees that they, like the elected officials, are public servants, and he humbly appealed to all employee unions to refrain from causing inconvenience to the people of Punjab, especially the farming community during this critical agricultural period.
The PSPCL employees commenced their strike on July 21, leading to considerable inconvenience for the public at a time when the paddy transplantation season is at a crucial stage. Arora noted that some demands have already been met. For the remaining issues, he highlighted that the employee unions themselves had requested the formation of a special committee involving representation from both the government and the unions.
